name: System Prompt Injection Templates Interface
description: Provides register-specific system prompt templates for normalizing user input across different communication registers (casual, academic, narrative, technical, direct). Implements Level 1 system prompt injection to ensure consistent technical interpretation regardless of input framing.

types.name: Register
types.description: Register enum type representing communication registers with .value attribute

functions.name: get_system_prompt
functions.description: Retrieves the appropriate Level 1 system prompt for a detected register. Returns register-specific normalization instructions from _REGISTER_PROMPTS dictionary, or GENERIC_NORMALIZATION as fallback. Returns empty string for 'direct' register.

inputs.name: detected_register
inputs.description: The detected communication register, either as string or Register enum

inputs.name: target_register
inputs.description: Optional target register (unused in current implementation)

postconditions: Returns empty string if detected_register is 'direct'
Returns register-specific prompt if detected_register in _REGISTER_PROMPTS
Return value is always a string (never None)

functions.name: inject_system_prompt
functions.description: Prepends a register normalization instruction to an existing system prompt. Idempotent: if the injection is already present in existing_system, returns unchanged. Handles empty string cases gracefully.

inputs.name: existing_system
inputs.description: The existing system prompt to inject into

inputs.name: injection
inputs.description: The text to inject/prepend to the existing system prompt

postconditions: Returns existing_system unchanged if injection is empty/falsy
Returns injection if existing_system is empty/falsy
Returns existing_system unchanged if injection already present (substring match)
Function is idempotent: inject_system_prompt(inject_system_prompt(a, b), b) == inject_system_prompt(a, b)

invariants: GENERIC_NORMALIZATION is a non-empty constant string
get_system_prompt always returns a string (never None)
inject_system_prompt is idempotent for any given (existing_system, injection) pair
